project: Dynamic Workflows CLI Validate And Durable Session List
description: Add CLI loopback behavior for dynamic JavaScript workflows so customers can validate workflow source and list durable Factory Sessions with stable human-readable and JSON output before the full runtime or HTTP parity path is complete.

context.customerAsk: Add CLI validation and durable session list loopback for dynamic workflows. CLI validation must succeed for a valid simple JavaScript workflow fixture and return blocking diagnostics for syntax errors, unsupported globals, invalid args schema, and policy-denied host access. CLI list output must show durable JavaScript Factory Session rows with status, source identity, result availability, phase/progress summary, and action availability when present. JSON output must be stable enough for tests and use generated or shared API/domain shapes where appropriate. Focused CLI tests must cover human output, JSON output, invalid input, and provider/service failure.
context.problem: Dynamic workflow work needs a fast, customer-testable CLI path. Users currently cannot rely on the CLI to validate JavaScript workflow source with stable diagnostics or list durable Factory Sessions with live, persisted, and all-session views that expose session status and result availability.
context.solution: Add command behavior for workflow source validation using existing source-kind, source-ref, and inline-source inputs, and extend CLI session listing to surface durable Factory Session summaries from deterministic provider data. Use the mock session-provider path first, or an equivalent direct factorysessionexecution.Service implementation, while keeping the command output contract stable for a later real service or HTTP API swap.

acceptanceCriteria: CLI validation succeeds for a valid simple JavaScript workflow fixture and exits successfully for both human-readable and JSON output.
CLI validation returns blocking diagnostics for syntax errors, unsupported globals or host access, invalid args schema, and policy-denied host access with stable machine-readable fields.
CLI session list output shows durable JavaScript Factory Session rows with lifecycle status, source identity, result availability, phase or progress summary, and action availability when present.
CLI session listing supports durable session scopes for live, persisted, and all sessions when the current command structure supports scoped listing.
JSON output for validation and listing is stable enough for tests and uses generated or shared API/domain shapes where appropriate rather than duplicating ad hoc response models.
Provider or service failure is reported as a clear CLI error with a non-zero exit and without partial misleading success output.
Quality gate: typecheck, lint, and focused CLI tests pass, including go test ./pkg/cli/workflow ./pkg/cli/session ./pkg/cli.

userStories.title: Validate a simple JavaScript workflow from CLI inputs
userStories.description: As a workflow author, I want to validate a simple JavaScript workflow source from the CLI so I can confirm the source is acceptable before starting a Factory Session.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid simple JavaScript workflow fixture validates successfully from a supported source input path such as source kind plus source ref or inline source.
Human output clearly reports that validation passed and includes safe source identity details when available.
JSON output reports a successful validation result with stable source identity, source hash when available, and an empty blocking diagnostics collection.
The validation command uses shared source normalization and validation behavior where available, not a separate CLI-only parser contract.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Report blocking JavaScript validation diagnostics
userStories.description: As a workflow author, I want CLI validation to reject invalid JavaScript workflow sources with clear blocking diagnostics so I can fix source, schema, and policy issues before execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Syntax errors return a non-zero exit and at least one blocking diagnostic with stable code, severity, message, and source location when available.
Unsupported globals or forbidden host access return blocking diagnostics without executing workflow source.
Invalid args schema returns a blocking diagnostic that identifies the args schema problem rather than a generic command failure.
Policy-denied host access returns a blocking diagnostic that distinguishes policy denial from syntax or schema failure.
Human output groups or labels blocking diagnostics in a readable way; JSON output preserves the same cases in stable machine-readable fields.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: List durable JavaScript Factory Sessions in human output
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the supported session-listing CLI path to show durable JavaScript Factory Sessions in human-readable output so I can inspect current and historical workflow sessions from the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: Human list output includes durable JavaScript Factory Session rows from deterministic provider data.
Each durable row shows session id, lifecycle status, safe source identity, result availability, phase or progress summary, and action availability when present.
Live, persisted, and all-session scopes are supported when the current command structure exposes scoped listing options.
Empty durable result sets produce a clear empty state that distinguishes a reachable provider with no matching sessions from a provider failure.
Legacy live-session list behavior remains compatible for existing live session rows.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Provide stable JSON list output for durable sessions
userStories.description: As an automation user, I want durable Factory Session list JSON to use stable shared shapes so scripts and future HTTP parity tests can consume list output without scraping human tables.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON list output includes durable JavaScript Factory Session summaries with status, source identity, result availability, phase or progress summary, and action availability when present.
JSON list output preserves live, persisted, and all-session scope behavior and deterministic ordering from the provider or shared normalizer.
JSON fields use generated API types, shared apisurface, or factorysessionexecution shapes where appropriate instead of a divergent CLI-only schema.
JSON output omits unrestricted host paths, raw workflow source, and secret-bearing provider internals.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Handle invalid input and provider failures consistently
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want invalid command input and provider or service failures to return clear errors and non-zero exits so automation can distinguish bad requests from unavailable execution infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing or conflicting validation source inputs fail before provider invocation with a clear command error and non-zero exit.
Unsupported session-list scope values fail with a clear command error and non-zero exit.
Provider or service validation failures return a clear CLI error without emitting a successful validation result.
Provider or service session-list failures return a clear CLI error without emitting partial success rows.
JSON error output, when requested by the existing command structure, is stable enough for focused CLI tests.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Preserve compatibility wording while steering users to Factory Sessions
userStories.description: As a user migrating from workflow preview commands, I want compatibility paths to keep working while new validation and listing behavior uses Factory Session execution terminology.
acceptanceCriteria: Legacy workflow preview command behavior remains compatibility-only and does not become the primary wording for durable execution list behavior.
New or changed CLI human output refers to Factory Sessions, session status, source identity, results, and actions rather than introducing a canonical dynamic workflow run noun.
Existing compatibility command tests continue to pass or are updated only for intentional terminology changes that preserve behavior.
Focused CLI tests cover human output, JSON output, invalid input, and provider/service failure for the new behavior.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
